12.title: …もの／もんだから
12.structure: Verb/Adj (Plain) / Noun な + もの／もんだから
12.explanation: Indicates the reason or cause of something, often used to justify it, or give a reason for it in order to deny responsibility or excuse oneself.

examples.jp: 急いでいたものですから、かぎをかけるのを忘れてしまいました。
examples.en: I was in a rush, so I went and forgot to lock up.

examples.jp: とても安かったものだから、買いすぎたんです。
examples.en: It was very cheap, so I bought too much.

12.summary: もの／もんだから gives a reason, often used to justify or excuse the speaker's own behavior — もんだから is the more casual, contracted spoken form.
12.details:
急いでいた**ものですから**、かぎをかけるのを忘れてしまいました。
*(I was in a rush, so I forgot to lock up.)*
とても安かった**ものだから**、買いすぎたんです。
*(It was very cheap, so I bought too much.)*

This pattern has a distinctly excuse-making or self-justifying flavor — compared with plain から, もの／もんだから frames the cause as an unavoidable circumstance the speaker feels shouldn't be held against them. もんだから is the contracted, more casual spoken equivalent of もの／ものだから.

14.title: 〜といった
14.structure: Noun 1, Noun 2... + といった + Noun 3
14.explanation: Indicates that N1, N2 etc. are specific examples of N3. It implies that there are also other examples apart from those mentioned.

examples.jp: 5月5日には「ちまき」「かしわもち」といった昔からの菓子を食べる習慣がある。
examples.en: On 5th May, there is the custom of eating traditional confectionery such as 'chimaki' and 'kashiwamochi'.

examples.jp: この大学にはルーマニア、ポーランドといった東ヨーロッパからの留学生が多い。
examples.en: There are many students from Eastern European countries such as Romania and Poland at this university.

14.summary: といった lists a couple of representative examples of a broader category, implying there are more items like them not mentioned.
14.details:
5月5日には「ちまき」「かしわもち」**といった**昔からの菓子を食べる習慣がある。
*(On May 5th, there's a custom of eating traditional sweets such as chimaki and kashiwamochi.)*

Structurally: N1、N2 ＋ といった ＋ N3, where N1/N2 are specific examples and N3 is the category they belong to (お菓子, 留学生, etc.). Compare with the N4 とか、とか point, which lists examples in casual speech — といった is the more formal, written equivalent used for the same purpose.

14.title: 〜に（も）わたって
14.explanation: Indicates that the speaker feels that the span of time mentioned is lengthy or the area extensive.

examples.jp: 手術は3時間にわたって行われた。
examples.en: The operation lasted for three hours.

examples.jp: 砂漠は東西450キロにわたって広がっている。
examples.en: The desert extends 450 km across from East to West.

14.summary: に（も）わたって marks that a span of time or area is felt to be notably long or extensive — used to emphasize scale.
14.details:
手術は3時間**にわたって**行われた。 *(The operation lasted for three hours.)*
砂漠は東西450キロ**にわたって**広がっている。 *(The desert extends 450 km from east to west.)*

The optional も (に**も**わたって) adds extra emphasis on just how long/extensive the span is — this pattern is reserved for spans the speaker genuinely considers noteworthy in scale (a multi-hour surgery, a huge desert), not routine short durations.

16.title: 〜に応じて
16.structure: Noun + に応じて / Noun 1 + に応じた + Noun 2
16.explanation: Indicates doing something appropriately 'in response to' a demand or request. When used with a word representing change or diversity, it means 'in response to the change/diversity'.

examples.jp: 学生たちは大学に授業料についての要求をしました。1年間話し合った後、大学は要求に応じました。
examples.en: The students made demands about the tuition fees. After discussing it for a year, the university acceded to their demands.

examples.jp: 時代の変化に応じて若者の文化や考え方も変わる。
examples.en: Young people's culture and thinking also change in response to the changing times.

16.summary: に応じて means acting appropriately 'in response to' something — a demand, a request, or a changing situation — adjusting behavior to match.
16.details:
学生たちは大学に授業料についての要求をしました。1年間話し合った後、大学は要求**に応じました**。
*(The students made demands about tuition. After a year of talks, the university acceded to their demands.)*
時代の変化**に応じて**若者の文化や考え方も変わる。 *(Young people's culture also changes in response to the changing times.)*

When paired with a word implying variation or diversity (変化, 個人, ニーズ), に応じて conveys "adapting to match" that variation — the response scales or adjusts according to what it's responding to, rather than being a single fixed reaction.

16.title: 〜にもかかわらず
16.structure: Verb/Adj (Plain) / Noun (である) + にもかかわらず
16.explanation: Indicates an action or event occurring despite contrary expectations. It carries a similar meaning to '〜のに' but is more formal.

examples.jp: 雨が激しく降っているにもかかわらず、サッカーの試合は行われた。
examples.en: Despite the heavy rain, the soccer match was held.

examples.jp: 彼は熱があるにもかかわらず、仕事へ行きました。
examples.en: In spite of having a fever, he went to work.

16.summary: にもかかわらず means 'despite' or 'in spite of' — similar to のに, but more formal, and typically found in writing or formal speech.
16.details:
雨が激しく降っている**にもかかわらず**、サッカーの試合は行われた。
*(Despite the heavy rain, the soccer match was held.)*
彼は熱がある**にもかかわらず**、仕事へ行きました。 *(In spite of having a fever, he went to work.)*

See the N4 のに point for the more conversational equivalent of this same contrastive meaning — にもかかわらず carries the same "contrary to expectation" nuance but reads as noticeably more formal, and doesn't carry のに's stronger emotional undertone of complaint/reproach.

16.title: 〜ところだった
16.meaning: Was just about to / Almost happened
16.structure: Verb (Dictionary form) + ところだった
16.explanation: Used to express that a situation (often negative or dangerous) was just about to happen, but was narrowly avoided.

examples.jp: もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところだった。
examples.en: I was just about to miss the train (but I made it).

examples.jp: あやうく事故を起こすところだった。
examples.en: I almost caused an accident.

16.summary: ところだった says a (usually negative or dangerous) situation was on the verge of happening, but was narrowly avoided.
16.details:
もう少しで電車に乗り遅れる**ところだった**。 *(I was just about to miss the train — but I made it.)*
あやうく事故を起こす**ところだった**。 *(I almost caused an accident.)*

Often paired with adverbs emphasizing how close a call it was — もう少しで ("just a little more and..."), あやうく ("narrowly") — the whole point of the sentence is relief that the bad outcome was avoided at the last moment. Contrast with the plain V dictionary form + ところだ／ところです ("about to..."), which doesn't carry that same narrowly-averted, past-tense nuance.

17.title: 〜からには
17.meaning: Because X, then of course Y / Now that...
17.structure: Verb (Plain) / Noun (である) + からには
17.explanation: Means 'because X is a fact, then naturally Y'. The 'Y' part is often an expression of a strong determination, order, obligation, or aspiration.

examples.jp: 大学院に入ったからには、どんなに大変でも学位を取って国へ帰りたい。
examples.en: Now that I've gotten into graduate school, I want to get my degree and go back home no matter how tough it is.

examples.jp: やるからには勝たなければならないと思う。
examples.en: As long as I'm doing it, I feel I have to win.

17.summary: からには means 'because X is now a settled fact, Y naturally follows' — the second clause typically expresses strong resolve, obligation, or aspiration.
17.details:
大学院に入った**からには**、どんなに大変でも学位を取って国へ帰りたい。
*(Now that I've gotten into graduate school, I want to get my degree and go home, however tough it is.)*
やる**からには**勝たなければならないと思う。 *(As long as I'm doing it, I feel I have to win.)*

Unlike a neutral cause-and-effect (から), からには implies a decision or commitment already made, and the second half is the natural, almost obligatory consequence of that commitment — it's frequently paired with strong resolve verbs (たい, なければならない).

17.title: 〜ざるを得ない
17.meaning: Cannot help but / Have no choice but to
17.structure: Verb (ない form, drop ない) + ざるを得ない (※する -> せざるを得ない)
17.explanation: Indicates that one does not want to do something, but has absolutely no other choice due to the circumstances.

examples.jp: 熱が39度もあるので、今日の会議は休まざるを得ない。
examples.en: Since I have a fever of 39 degrees, I have no choice but to miss today's meeting.

examples.jp: 電車が止まってしまったので、歩いて帰らざるを得ない。
examples.en: Because the trains have stopped, I cannot help but walk home.

17.summary: ざるを得ない means having no real choice but to do something the speaker doesn't actually want to do — 'cannot help but...'
17.details:
熱が39度もあるので、今日の会議は休ま**ざるを得ない**。
*(Since I have a 39-degree fever, I have no choice but to miss today's meeting.)*
電車が止まってしまったので、歩いて帰ら**ざるを得ない**。
*(Because the trains have stopped, I can't help but walk home.)*

Formed from the ない-form (drop ない) + ざるを得ない — irregular for する, which becomes せざるを得ない (not しざるを得ない). The whole phrase always carries reluctance: the speaker is being forced into an action by circumstances, against their actual preference.

17.title: 〜からなる
17.structure: Noun + からなる / からなっている
17.explanation: A formal expression used to describe what parts, elements, or materials make up a whole entity.

examples.jp: この本は、10の章からなっている。
examples.en: This book is composed of 10 chapters.

examples.jp: 水は水素と酸素からなる。
examples.en: Water consists of hydrogen and oxygen.

17.summary: からなる is a formal expression describing what components make up a whole — 'consists of' or 'is composed of.'
17.details:
この本は、10の章**からなっている**。 *(This book is composed of 10 chapters.)*
水は水素と酸素**からなる**。 *(Water consists of hydrogen and oxygen.)*

This is a written, somewhat technical/encyclopedic register — natural for describing the composition of a system, document, or substance (chapters of a book, elements of a compound, members of an organization), but not something you'd casually use in everyday conversation.

18.title: 〜ものの
18.structure: Verb/Adj (Plain) / Noun (である) + ものの
18.explanation: Indicates that although the first part (the premise) is true, the result in the second part is contrary to expectations or is not fully realized.

examples.jp: 新しいパソコンを買ったものの、使い方がわからない。
examples.en: Even though I bought a new PC, I don't know how to use it.

examples.jp: 日本語の勉強を始めたものの、なかなか上達しない。
examples.en: Although I started studying Japanese, I'm not making much progress.

18.summary: ものの concedes that the first statement is true, but the outcome that follows runs contrary to what you'd expect, or falls short of it.
18.details:
新しいパソコンを買った**ものの**、使い方がわからない。 *(Even though I bought a new PC, I don't know how to use it.)*
日本語の勉強を始めた**ものの**、なかなか上達しない。 *(Although I started studying Japanese, I'm not making much progress.)*

ものの has a similar concessive feel to のに (N4) and にもかかわらず, but reads as more neutral/literary — it doesn't carry のに's charge of complaint/reproach, just a calm acknowledgment that the outcome didn't match the premise's natural expectation.

19.title: 〜をめぐって／〜をめぐる
19.meaning: Concerning / Over / Regarding (a dispute or discussion)
19.structure: Noun + をめぐって / Noun + をめぐる + Noun
19.explanation: Used when multiple people are arguing, discussing, or competing 'over' or 'concerning' a central issue. It is used in news or formal contexts.

examples.jp: 新しい法律をめぐって、激しい議論が交わされている。
examples.en: Intense debates are being exchanged over the new law.

examples.jp: 遺産をめぐる争いが起きた。
examples.en: A dispute over the inheritance occurred.

19.summary: をめぐって marks the central issue that people are arguing, discussing, or competing over — 'concerning/over [a contested topic].'
19.details:
新しい法律**をめぐって**、激しい議論が交わされている。 *(Intense debates are being exchanged over the new law.)*
遺産**をめぐる**争いが起きた。 *(A dispute over the inheritance occurred.)*

をめぐって is reserved specifically for situations involving conflict, debate, or competing interests around a shared topic — different from a neutral topic marker like について (N3), which just introduces what something is about without implying any dispute.

20.title: 〜からいうと／〜からいえば／〜からいって
20.meaning: Judging from / From the standpoint of
20.structure: Noun + からいうと／からいえば／からいって
20.explanation: Used to make a judgment or evaluation based on a specific standpoint, symptom, or piece of evidence.

examples.jp: 現状からいうと、計画の変更は避けられない。
examples.en: Judging from the current situation, a change of plans is unavoidable.

examples.jp: 消費者の立場からいえば、値段は安いほうがいい。
examples.en: From the standpoint of consumers, cheaper prices are better.

20.summary: からいうと／からいえば／からいって all mark the standpoint or evidence a judgment is being made from — 'judging from...'
20.details:
現状**からいうと**、計画の変更は避けられない。 *(Judging from the current situation, a change of plans is unavoidable.)*
消費者の立場**からいえば**、値段は安いほうがいい。 *(From consumers' standpoint, cheaper prices are better.)*

All three variants (からいうと／からいえば／からいって) are interchangeable, attaching to a noun that represents the vantage point or body of evidence behind the following judgment. Compare with にとって (N3), which marks a perspective for evaluating something's *importance/difficulty*, whereas からいうと marks the *basis* for a specific conclusion or prediction.

21.title: 〜といえども
21.structure: Noun / Plain form + といえども
21.explanation: An archaic/formal expression meaning '〜といっても' or '〜ではあるが'. Used to state that despite a fact or condition, something else holds true.

examples.jp: どんな大金持ちといえども、お金で解決できない悩みがあるはずだ。
examples.en: However rich one might be, there are bound to be some problems that money can't solve.

examples.jp: 名医といえども、すべての患者を救うことはできない。
examples.en: However skillful a doctor might be, she cannot save all her patients.

21.summary: といえども is an archaic/formal way of saying 'even though X, still Y' — roughly equivalent to といっても or ではあるが, but reserved for formal or written register.
21.details:
どんな大金持ち**といえども**、お金で解決できない悩みがあるはずだ。
*(However rich one might be, there are bound to be problems money can't solve.)*
名医**といえども**、すべての患者を救うことはできない。
*(However skillful a doctor might be, she cannot save all her patients.)*

This carries a classical, almost proverbial tone — often used with extreme examples (大金持ち, 名医) to make a broad, memorable point. In everyday conversation, というても or ではあるが would be the natural, less formal substitutes for the same underlying "even granting X, still Y" logic.

21.title: N ＋ に基づいて
21.structure: Noun + に基づいて / に基づいた + Noun
21.explanation: Means 'based on ~'. When modifying a noun directly, it takes the form '〜に基づいた'.

examples.jp: この映画は、事実に基づいて作られている。
examples.en: This film is based on true facts.

examples.jp: デパートでは、調査結果に基づいた新しいサービスを導入した。
examples.en: The department store introduced some new services based on the results of a survey.

21.summary: に基づいて means 'based on' — grounding something in a stated source, fact, or set of results — with に基づいた used to modify a following noun directly.
21.details:
この映画は、事実**に基づいて**作られている。 *(This film is based on true facts.)*
デパートでは、調査結果**に基づいた**新しいサービスを導入した。 *(The department store introduced new services based on survey results.)*

Structurally straightforward: に基づいて attaches mid-sentence (like a て-form connector), while に基づいた attaches directly before a noun it modifies — the same shape distinction you've already seen with による／によって (N3) and に関する／に関して (N3).

21.title: 〜が、一方で
21.meaning: But, at the same time / On the other hand
21.explanation: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with a preceding statement.

examples.jp: 日本は技術が進んだ国だが、一方で古い伝統文化も大切にしている。
examples.en: Japan is a technologically-advanced country, but at the same time it cherishes its traditional culture.

21.summary: が、一方で introduces a statement that contrasts with what was just said — 'but, on the other hand' or 'while at the same time.'
21.details:
日本は技術が進んだ国だ**が、一方で**古い伝統文化も大切にしている。
*(Japan is a technologically advanced country, but at the same time it cherishes its traditional culture.)*

一方で highlights that two seemingly contrasting facts are both simultaneously true about the same subject — useful for essay writing and balanced arguments where you want to acknowledge two sides of something without one negating the other.

22.title: 〜次第だ / 〜次第で
22.structure: Verb (て-form / た-form) + 次第です
22.explanation: When ending with '次第です', it means 'for this reason, I did ~'. It's a formal way to explain circumstances. When used as '次第で', it means 'depending on'.

examples.jp: 関係者が情報を共有すべきだと考え、皆様にお知らせした次第です。
examples.en: We let everyone involved know about it because we believed the information should be shared.

examples.jp: 私どもだけではどうしようもなく、こうしてお願いに参った次第でございます。
examples.en: There's no way we can manage it by ourselves, so this is why we have come to ask you for a favor like this.

22.summary: 次第です explains circumstances formally ('for this reason, I did X'); 次第で instead means 'depending on' — two quite different meanings sharing the same word.
22.details:
### 次第だ (Explaining Circumstances) vs 次第で (Depending On)

| Form | Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **V て/た-form ＋ 次第です** | Formally explains why the speaker did something | 皆様にお知らせした**次第です**。 *(This is why we informed everyone.)* |
| **N ＋ 次第で** | "Depending on N" | 結果**次第で**、対応が変わります。 *(The response will change depending on the result.)* |

The 次第です form is quite formal and often appears at the very end of a business letter or formal explanation, summarizing the reasoning behind an action just described.

22.title: 〜をもって…とする
22.meaning: Regarded as / On the basis of
22.structure: Noun + をもって…とする / とされている
22.explanation: Indicates '〜を…と見なす' (is regarded as). This is a highly formal written expression.

examples.jp: 出席率、授業中の発表、レポートをもって、評価とします。
examples.en: Students are evaluated on the basis of attendance rate, presentations during classes, and reports.

examples.jp: 拍手をもって、賛成をいただいたものといたします。
examples.en: Based on your applause, I shall take it that I have received your endorsement.

22.summary: をもって…とする is a highly formal written expression meaning 'to regard X as...' or 'on the basis of X' — typically found in official announcements and formal declarations.
22.details:
出席率、授業中の発表、レポート**をもって**、評価**とします**。
*(Students are evaluated on the basis of attendance rate, in-class presentations, and reports.)*
拍手**をもって**、賛成をいただいたものと**いたします**。
*(Based on your applause, I shall take it that I have received your endorsement.)*

This is essentially a formal written equivalent of 〜を〜と見なす ("regard X as Y") — you'll encounter it in official rules, ceremony announcements, and formal business writing, rarely in everyday speech.

22.title: 〜におきましては
22.structure: Noun + においては / におきましては
22.explanation: An expression that defines the extent of something, and is an even more formal way of saying '〜では'. Often used in formal writing or speeches.

examples.jp: 経済成長期の日本においては、収入が2〜3年で倍になることもあった。
examples.en: In Japan during its rapid economic growth period, some people's incomes doubled within two to three years.

examples.jp: 小社におきましては、目下『私の死亡記事』というネクロロジー集を編集中です。
examples.en: At our company, we are currently compiling a collection of obituaries entitled 'My Obituary'.

22.summary: においては／におきましては is an even more formal way of saying では, defining the scope or context something applies within.
22.details:
経済成長期の日本**においては**、収入が2〜3年で倍になることもあった。
*(In Japan during its rapid economic growth period, some people's incomes doubled within two to three years.)*
小社**におきましては**、目下『私の死亡記事』というネクロロジー集を編集中です。
*(At our company, we are currently compiling a collection of obituaries titled "My Obituary.")*

におきましては is the more deferential/humble-sounding of the two, often used in business correspondence when referring to one's own company (小社におきましては) — においては is slightly less formal but still clearly written/formal register compared to plain では.

23.title: 〜に及ぶ
23.explanation: Indicates that what is expressed as the subject of the sentence extends as far as the stated scope, area, or time.

examples.jp: 害虫による松の被害は県内全域に及んでおり、回復には時間がかかるだろう。
examples.en: Insect damage to pine trees extends to all parts of the prefecture, and it will take time to recover.

examples.jp: 議論は国内問題にとどまらず国際問題にまで及び、実りのあるものとなった。
examples.en: The discussion was not confined to domestic issues but broadened out to include international ones, making it fruitful.

23.summary: に及ぶ says something extends as far as a stated scope, area, or time — emphasizing the reach or extent of the subject.
23.details:
害虫による松の被害は県内全域**に及んでおり**、回復には時間がかかるだろう。
*(Insect damage to pine trees extends across the whole prefecture, and recovery will take time.)*
議論は国内問題にとどまらず国際問題にまで**及び**、実りのあるものとなった。
*(The discussion wasn't confined to domestic issues but extended to international ones, becoming fruitful.)*

に及ぶ often pairs with にとどまらず ("not confined to...") to emphasize that something has spread well beyond an initially expected scope — a formal/written expression common in news reporting.

24.title: V-ない ＋ ざる N
24.structure: Verb (ない-form, drop ない) + ざる + Noun
24.explanation: An archaic form used when modifying a noun with 'Vない'. Since archaic forms remain only in stock expressions, their use is limited (e.g., 知られざる, 見ざる).

examples.jp: 歴史にはまだ知られざる事実があるはずだ。
examples.en: Many historical facts must still be unknown (facts that are not known).

examples.jp: 「見ざる、聞かざる、言わざる」は一つの生き方を示している。
examples.en: 'See nothing, hear nothing, say nothing' points to one way of living one's life.

24.summary: V-ない + ざる + N is an archaic noun-modifying form, surviving today only in a handful of fixed expressions.
24.details:
歴史にはまだ**知られざる**事実があるはずだ。 *(Many historical facts must still be unknown.)*
「**見ざる**、聞かざる、言わざる」は一つの生き方を示している。 *("See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil" points to one way of living.)*

This classical negative form (ざる, from the old auxiliary ず) once modified nouns the way ない does today (知らない事実 → 知られざる事実), but in modern Japanese it survives only in stock idioms and set phrases — you won't productively form new ざる expressions the way you can with ない, but recognizing them (見ざる聞かざる言わざる being the most famous) is useful for reading older or more literary text.

24.title: 〜から〜に至るまで
24.structure: Noun 1 + から + Noun 2 + に至るまで (にいたるまで)
24.explanation: By citing items at either extreme of a group, it indicates that something applies to absolutely everything in that group.

examples.jp: 自転車のねじから人工衛星の部品に至るまで、どれもこの工場で作っています。
examples.en: We make everything in this factory from bicycle screws to satellite components.

examples.jp: クラシックからJ-popに至るまで、当店ではどんなジャンルの音楽でもご用意しております。
examples.en: We offer all kinds of music in this shop, from classical to J-pop.

24.summary: から〜に至るまで cites two extreme ends of a group to emphasize that something applies to absolutely everything within it — 'from A all the way to Z.'
24.details:
自転車のねじから人工衛星の部品**に至るまで**、どれもこの工場で作っています。
*(We make everything in this factory, from bicycle screws all the way to satellite components.)*
クラシックからJ-pop**に至るまで**、当店ではどんなジャンルの音楽でもご用意しております。
